title.narrative: BRIDGE - Bridging Gaps in Essential Health Services in NES

description.narrative: ltpgtThe BRIDGE project seeks to reduce morbidity and mortality among crisis-affected populations by restoring their access to a comprehensive continuum of care this includes quality primary healthcare, life-saving secondary servicesnbspand a functional referral system that connects both levels of care. Nearly 3million people across NES are now at increased risk as public health facilities shut down and referral pathways break downnbspIDPs living in camps are especially vulnerable, facing high rates of trauma, maternal complications communicable diseases, and waterborne outbreaks like the cholera surge in Al-Hol campltbrgtThe project supports 13key health facilities operated by UPP-KRC: 6primary healthcare centers in IDP camps Areesha, Al Hol ph 1+4, Washokai, Serekaniye, and Abu Khashab,4 out-of-camp centers in Tel Tamer, Shadadi and Maabadeh in Hassake,nbspAr-Rasheed PHC.nbspand 1Ambulance Center facilitating emergency transfers in Raqqanbspand 2Ambulance Centers in Deir ez Zor (nbspKisreh and Maamel).nbspThrough the provision of essential medicines,medical consumables,and infection prevention supplies, the project ensures uninterrupted delivery of outpatient services, maternal and reproductive health (including safe deliveries), and trauma care. A co-financing approach allows this project to focus on medical inputs, while operational costs are covered by complementary programs. , BRIDGE facilitates public health surveillance. All facilities will submit weekly surveillance reports through the established WHO reporting channels, thereby contributing to early detection and response to disease outbreaks.ltbrgtTo ensure patients can access higher levels of care, BRIDGE invests in a strengthened referral system built around the UPP-KRC ambulance fleet which is fully equipped to stabilize and transfer patients in critical condition These ambulances connect primary health facilities with hospitals including HassakehnbspltbrgtNational Hospitalnbspthe main public secondary care provider in the Hassake governorate and the primary referral hub for the campsnbspHNH will be supported under a Health Equity Fund mechanism, which covers the full cost of surgical interventions,diagnostic tests, and treatment for IDPs referred from the camps this model eliminates out-of-pocket expenses and reactivates lifesaving services that had been inaccessible after funding was withdrawn in February 2025. HNH will provide much-needed surgical procedures for IDPs with progressive conditions that if left un-treated could become life-threatening or cause irreversible harm. t In cases where a required essential secondary service is not available at HNH, UPP will operationalize a case-based referral reimbursement mechanism, ensuring no patient from the camps is left behind due to service limitations. Hence referred patients will be treated at an alternative hospital such as the heart and eye hospital in Qamishlinbspand the costs will be reimbursed to the hospital by UPP following the same modality as for Hassake National hospital.ltbrgtBeyond emergency response, BRIDGE also contributes to health system resilience and sustainability by providing medical equipment to HNH and offering in-service training to clinical staff at supported facilities, the project strengthens the quality of care and rational use of medicinesnbspreducing misuse and improving adherence to international standards. Trainings cover reproductive and child healthnbsptrauma stabilization, communicable disease management, and emergency protocols.nbspThe project also supports disease prevention and response in camp settingsnbspIn the face of poor WASH conditionsnbspltbrgtBRIDGE will set up Oral Rehydration Points and stock emergency supplies to reduce deaths from diarrheal and waterborne diseases. The intervention leverages UPP’s strong field presence and logistics, ensuring fast delivery and consistent service quality.ltbrgtlt/pgt
